name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,571

clue.text: Smartphone I fixed for one who distrusts mankind

indicators.note: a phone that has been fixed has had its parts put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone repaired a smartphone for a person who hates humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope dislikes and mistrusts people generally, the human race as a whole.

clue.text: Political statement isn't finished: that's obvious

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a party's published programme of policies

explanation.surface: A complaint that a party's policy document is incomplete, which everyone can see.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means plain to see, clear or evident.

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly person is getting a swollen blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-timer' suggests a pensioner, but here it means someone from ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sumerians were among the earliest civilisations, living in ancient Mesopotamia thousands of years ago.

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the name before it
to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

explanation.surface: Lady Godiva goes for an unclothed run.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked through Coventry, which makes 'naked' look like part of her story.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow or memory is to give them a gentle push or prod.

clue.text: Looked around entrance to abbey frequented by spirits

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another
the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone peered round the door of an abbey said to be visited by ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunted building is one that ghosts are believed to visit or inhabit repeatedly.

clue.text: Watch Bobby regularly hit the ball

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: start a point in tennis by striking the ball

explanation.surface: Watch Bobby, who often hits the ball in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a player's name, or a British policeman, but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to look at closely, to keep an eye on something.

clue.text: Overhear what happens in autumn, but not the start

indicators.note: excluding the start means the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: in autumn, foliage falls from the trees

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what you overhear in the autumn season.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation, catching words not meant for you.

clue.text: Charity starts to advance international development

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

blocks.note: initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A charity begins to push forward global development work.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is help, money or supplies given to those in need, as charity provides.

clue.text: I agree to receive copper's insight

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: said to affirm a prayer: so be it
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to hear a police officer's shrewd observations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a British police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharp judgement and quick understanding, especially in business or practical matters.

blocks.note: a small private room for work

explanation.surface: A poet's tedious piece of academic research.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English writer, England's first Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Traveller is sensible to skip capital of Tunisia

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter
skipping something means leaving it out

explanation.surface: A traveller decides it is wise to avoid Tunis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Tunisia' wants to be Tunis; here it is just the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place with no fixed home, a perpetual wanderer.

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the adjective 'without savour'

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: lacking savour or flavour
second meaning: unpleasant or morally offensive

explanation.surface: A diner's outraged reaction to unseasoned food.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UN-SAVOURY, the word literally means not savoury, which is what food without salt is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word usually means unpleasant or objectionable, but literally describes food lacking any savoury taste.

clue.text: Hot-headed entertainer's achievement: concealing anger with the queen

indicators.note: concealing something means holding it hidden inside

explanation.surface: A short-tempered performer manages to hide fury in front of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot-headed' means quick-tempered in the surface, but in the definition it is literal: flames go in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-eater is a circus or street performer who puts flaming torches into their mouth.

indicators.note: taking something in by ear means hearing it, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: perceived means seen, which is said the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A disturbance noticed only through hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a scene is to cause a public fuss or angry disturbance.

clue.text: Frightened about conclusion of paper being marked

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
the conclusion of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A student is nervous about the end of an exam paper being graded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marked' suggests a teacher grading the paper; here it means bearing scars.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred skin or surfaces carry visible marks left by old wounds or damage.

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a pale piece of jewellery for a finger; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A remark that pale-coloured jewellery has a traditionalist look.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-wing politics favour tradition and established order, the outlook of political conservatives.

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: Musicians' auditory senses at work while practising.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the body parts we listen with, the organs of hearing.

indicators.note: to snare is to trap and hold, so one piece is caught inside another

blocks.note: a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A robbery catches a professor who lives for enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist pursues sensual enjoyment as life's main goal, devoted to indulgence.

indicators.note: to surround is to go all the way round, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Hannibal Lecter, the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs

explanation.surface: A history teacher describes the Carthaginian general besieging a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannibal' suggests the Carthaginian general who besieged cities, but it is the fictional serial killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer teaches by giving lectures, usually at a university or college.

indicators.note: odd characters are those in first, third, fifth and seventh positions

explanation.surface: Strange people from a North African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Algerian city' reads as one phrase, but Algerian is the source of letters and the definition is only 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a large Indian urban centre, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Fashion red coat in a particular style

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Make a scarlet jacket in a distinctive design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the clothes world; it is a verb meaning make.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s, known for geometric shapes.

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Electricity runs out during an industrial walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests workers downing tools; it means strike out text.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or exhaust a supply until little remains.

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun phrase

blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a television set that is dead

explanation.surface: A paradox: the television is repaired yet broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to contradict itself; 'Fixed' means determined, not repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dead set on a plan is resolute and unwavering; a dead set is also a television that will not work.

blocks.note: first meaning: goods kept ready for use

explanation.definitionFit: A shop's goods on hand and an investor's shares in companies are both called by this word.

clue.text: Decide what to show member of the clergy

blocks.note: first meaning: select items for an exhibition
second meaning: an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.walkthrough: One word, two pronunciations: the verb stresses the second syllable, the churchman the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum organiser selects exhibits; separately, a parish assistant priest in the Church of England holds this title.

indicators.note: after says which piece follows, so the second word comes later in the answer

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Religious belief erodes as years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is confident belief or reliance on someone, much as faith is.

blocks.note: first meaning: carry from place to place
second meaning: overwhelming joy, a rapture

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to carry goods or people; the noun, often plural, means an ecstatic emotional rapture.

clue.text: Instrument is brought back by sailor

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the word reads the other direction

blocks.note: an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor returns home carrying a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked Indian string instrument with many strings.

indicators.note: devious means crooked and indirect, so the letters go in a twisted order

explanation.surface: A thief's sneaky tools of the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instruments' looks like burglary tools; they are woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarinets are single-reed woodwind musical devices played in orchestras and bands.

definitions.note: the whole phrase stands for the person in the saying

blocks.note: first meaning: the old city on the Moselle
second meaning: from the saying 'God loves a ...', praising someone who makes an effort

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'God loves a trier' encourages anyone who has a go, even unsuccessfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is a historic Roman city in western Germany; a trier is also anyone who keeps attempting things.

definitions.note: an example standing for the noun

blocks.note: second meaning: a bishop's diocese, of which Canterbury is one

explanation.surface: Catch sight of the cathedral city of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to spot visually; the noun is the area under a bishop's authority, such as Canterbury.

clue.text: King imprisons worthiest novel's unacknowledged author

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
to imprison is to shut inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Georgius Rex, King George's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch locks up the author of the most deserving book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the anagram signal; the definition just happens to fit a book's hidden writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter writes books or speeches published under someone else's name, receiving no public credit.
